words.meaning: not relevant or suitable for the situation
words.example: The comparison to last year's launch is inapposite because the market conditions have changed completely.

words.meaning: limited by conditions, exceptions, or reservations
words.example: The legal team gave the proposal qualified approval pending one change to the contract.

words.meaning: less important than, but connected to, the main issue or purpose
words.example: Cost is a subsidiary concern; our first priority is protecting customer data.

words.meaning: caused by one's own avoidable mistake rather than outside pressure
words.example: Sending the draft without checking the attachment was an unforced error.

words.meaning: having a strong personal interest in a particular outcome
words.example: Team leads are vested in making the new review process work because it will save them hours each week.

phrases.meaning: something that creates a favorable impression or shows good judgment
phrases.example: Giving the support crew credit in the presentation was a good look.

phrases.meaning: to understand or become aware of what everyone else already knows
phrases.example: Apparently I didn't get the memo that everyone was working from home today.

phrases.meaning: said when an idea or situation has become much more appealing
phrases.example: A four-day weekend with no email? Now we're talking.

phrases.meaning: an emphatic way to say that you strongly agree, usually because you have the same experience
phrases.example: This traffic is brutal. You're telling me—I've been stuck here for an hour.

phrases.meaning: said when a person appears just after being mentioned
phrases.example: Speak of the devil—Marcus just walked in while we were discussing his proposal.
